description: Syntax Prefilter blocked by FIXTURE_TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE predicts a later seat (scar_chronicler) blocked the same way

lesson.applicability: Runs where an early seat observation has blocked=true and failure_code FIXTURE_TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE with the summary 'No model was sent'. This applies to runs with the openrouter executor.
lesson.cause: FIXTURE_TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE is a run-level transport condition, not a seat-specific fault. No model request is sent, so every subsequent seat that needs the transport is blocked the same way.
lesson.correction: Treat the first FIXTURE_TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE block as run-wide. Do not plan work that depends on model output from later seats. Either restore the fixture transport before dispatching further seats or record the run as blocked with that residual.
lesson.exceptions: Does not apply if the transport is restored or replaced between seat dispatches. It also does not apply to blocks with other failure codes, such as provider HTTP errors or an unavailable native gate.
lesson.failed_claim: The assumption that a later seat can still run and produce model output after the first seat was blocked by a missing fixture transport.
lesson.verification: Host replay of recorded host facts over 48 runs: the detector fired in 5 and the outcome followed every time. Proposed by claude-sonnet-5-5. This does not rerun the old checks or show that the guidance helps later runs.

predicate: The recorded outcome {"kind": "SEAT_BLOCKED"} is anticipated and handled before it occurs.

trigger: A Adversary seat observation matching {"blocked": true, "failure_code": "FIXTURE_TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE", "role": "syntax_prefilter"}
